key_insight: Acoustic forcing can drive very different mesoscale flame regimes into a common oscillatory extinction-ignition state (O-FREI), with stronger forcing lowering mean heat release while boosting forcing-frequency oscillations.
engineering_relevance: This matters for designing compact combustors, micro-propulsion, and portable power systems because pressure-driven instabilities can directly alter flame stability, efficiency, and reliability.
method: Applied upstream acoustic forcing at the combustor first harmonic.
Compared three flame regimes: FREI, stable flames, and propagating flames.
Used reduced-order mathematical models to interpret the observed response.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a broad sweep of acoustic pressure intensities and identifies consistent transitions in flame behavior, heat release rate, and Strouhal number across all regimes.
watch_item: The reported trends are specific to the tested mesoscale combustor and forcing conditions, so transfer to other geometries or operating points should be validated before design use.
paper_title: Response of Confined Mesoscale Flames to Acoustic Forcing
